title: molopospermum cicutarium
intro: Molopospermum cicutarium, commonly known as hoary cress or wild mustard, is a biennial plant in the Brassicaceae family native to Europe and Asia, but now found in many other regions. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antibacterial properties, which can help to alleviate symptoms of colds, fever, and respiratory issues. The therapeutic actions of hoary cress include acting as an expectorant, demulcent, and diuretic, making it useful for treating coughs, sore throats, and urinary problems. The bioactive constituents of Molopospermum cicutarium include isothiocyanates, which have been shown to have antioxidant and anticancer properties, as well as glucosinolates, which have been found to have anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects.
